waiting.description:
The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 remains the shortest recorded war in history. On August 27, 1896, Sultan Khalid bin Barghash seized power in Zanzibar Town without British approval, barricading 2,800 men inside the seafront palace complex. Royal Navy warships under Rear-Admiral Harry Rawson opened fire at 09:02 AM, sinking the royal yacht HHS Glasgow and ending the entire conflict by 09:46 AM. Could any modern military conflict ever end this quickly?

waiting.description:
How Quetzalcoatlus flight worked has fascinated paleontologists since 1971. Discovered in Big Bend National Park, Texas, by Douglas Lawson, this giant azhdarchid pterosaur lived during the Late Cretaceous period. Biomechanical models show it launched quadrupedally by vaulting off powerful wing muscles rather than running. Could a creature this massive survive in modern skies?

waiting.topic: Tyrannosaurus lived closer in time to humans than to Stegosaurus

waiting.description:
Tyrannosaurus lived closer in time to humans than to Stegosaurus. While pop culture constantly pairs them together, T. rex roamed North America sixty-six million years ago, whereas Stegosaurus vanished nearly eighty million years prior. First uncovered in Colorado during the nineteenth-century Bone Wars, these iconic giants never shared the Earth. Which prehistoric timeline surprise shocked you the most?
